learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of Linear Algebra.
Basic knowledge on the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in Engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and technologies, as well as providing them with great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the activity of the Telecommunication Technical Engineer.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, task planning and other similar works in their specific field of telecommunications.
Use the basic properties of real and complex numbers and perform fundamental operations with them.
Use the basic elements of Linear Algebra: systems of linear equations, vector spaces and linear applications and use matrices to simplify their study.
Identify metric properties in vector spaces, through the scalar product, norm, or distance.
Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors and diagonalize endomorphisms and matrices.
Solve geometric problems in the plane and in space.

syllabus_topics: Systems of linear equations and matrices.
Introduction to differential equations and systems of linear differential equations.

assessment_methods.method: Written exams (two exams, first on first three topics, second on remaining topics, second exam also allows for resit of first exam)

assessment_rules: The final grade (CF) is calculated using the formula: CF = 0.15*PL + maximum ( 0.15*PA+0.7*PE , 0.85*PE ). PE is the final grade for written tests, PA for classroom practices, and PL for laboratory practices. A minimum score of 2.5 out of 10 is required on each written test; if not achieved, the final grade will be the minimum of CF and 4.5. Non-attendance at the official ordinary exam results in a 'NO PRESENTADO' (No Show) grade.
